# xgbexcel

> xgbexcel converts trained XGBRegressor or XGBClassifier models into Excel formula expressions. This enables deploying XGBoost models directly in Excel spreadsheets without any programming environment.

## Key Facts

- Converts XGBoost models (regressor and classifier) to Excel IF-formula expressions
- Supports multi-class classification with softmax
- Feature renaming for human-readable Excel formulas
- Save expressions to file
- Works with xgboost==1.7.1 (XGBoost 2.0+ vector leaves not yet supported)
- Installable via pip: `pip install xgbexcel`
- MIT licensed, Python 3.8+

## When to Use xgbexcel

- You need to deploy an XGBoost model in Excel without Python
- You want to share a trained ML model with non-technical stakeholders via a spreadsheet
- You need an interpretable formula representation of an XGBoost model
- You want to convert gradient boosting predictions into Excel-native calculations

## Links

- Repository: https://github.com/KalinNonchev/xgbexcel
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/xgbexcel/

## Installation

```
pip install xgbexcel
```

## Quick Start

```python
from xgbexcel import XGBtoExcel
from xgboost import XGBRegressor
import numpy as np

# Train a model
model = XGBRegressor().fit(X_train, y_train)

# Convert to Excel formula
excel = XGBtoExcel(model)
print(excel.expression)

# Rename features for readability
excel.rename_features({"x1": "Age", "x2": "Income"})

# Save to file
excel.save_expr("model_formula.txt")
```
